headline: High: Flowise can write shared files and egress broadly, creating default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks against great_expectations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while great_expectations consumes files for data sources, validation results, and documentation. That creates a plausible shared-file prompt-injection bridge if Flowise writes attacker-controlled content that GE later parses as trusted input. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Flowise writes content into a directory that great_expectations later reads as data or documentation, injection is possible.
IF great_expectations parses Flowise-produced text as authoritative instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories with OS permissions.
Require a human review step before GE consumes any Flowise-generated file.
Use allowlisted file formats only for handoff.
Add a checksum or provenance tag to every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials and has broad network egress; great_expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. If they share a workspace, Flowise can expose sensitive inputs or outputs through files or outbound tools, while GE can surface those artifacts in reports. The interaction is plausible from profiles alone, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or uploaded-file workspace, leakage becomes plausible.
IF Flowise tools send file contents to external model or HTTP providers, sensitive data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Store secrets and data files in separate mounts.
Disable or restrict Flowise HTTP/search tools for sensitive runs.
Redact secrets before any file handoff.
Review outbound destinations in Flowise flows.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the filesystem and uses server-datastore shared state across instances; great_expectations reads and writes files for validation artifacts. Even without explicit git or OAuth overlap, both can mutate shared files, so concurrent writes can collide in default deployments. The profiles support a real conflict pathway, though not a high-severity one.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or datastore, write collisions can occur.
IF Flowise instances run concurrently with GE artifact generation, last-write-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Snapshot outputs before GE writes reports.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add transactional storage or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces graph-based tool outputs, and great_expectations can consume validation inputs and documentation artifacts. If GE treats Flowise-generated content as authoritative without verification, a bad upstream result can cascade into incorrect validation or reporting. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF great_expectations ingests Flowise-generated files as validation inputs, upstream errors can propagate.
IF no human or schema verification occurs between agents, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a schema check before GE consumes Flowise output.
Require manual approval for any Flowise-generated dataset or config.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Log provenance for every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials and may process chatflow inputs/outputs, while great_expectations handles data sources, validation results, and documentation. A compliance issue exists only if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow; the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. Because the other agent is not clearly implicated in a specific violation, only the relevant profile fields are cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents without a documented retention policy, compliance risk increases.
IF Flowise stores secrets or chatflow outputs alongside GE validation artifacts, retention mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Keep regulated datasets out of Flowise flows unless necessary.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
Document deletion/export handling for validation outputs.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems.
